title: Airtable Shopify Integration Without Code
summary: Airtable Shopify integration copies your store's orders and products into Airtable bases. Set one up without code using Activepieces.
body_markdown:
## Five Shopify and Airtable Workflows in Activepieces


When you build the order-to-record sync in Activepieces, five workflows cover it, and only the fifth needs the webhook or HTTP request step the builder's gaps call for.


The table gives each flow's trigger, action and job, so you can see which ones run on listed steps alone.


Shopify trigger Airtable action Job done Webhook/HTTP step needed?


"New Order" "Create Airtable Record" One row per order No


"New Customer" "Find Airtable Record", then "Create Airtable Record" Customer list without duplicates No


"Updated Product" "Update Airtable Record" Product table stays current No


"New Paid Order" "Create Airtable Record" High-value orders land in a review view No


None listed (refunds) "Update Airtable Record" Mark an order refunded Yes


*Prices and plan limits checked against[activepieces.com](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/shopify) and[activepieces.com](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/airtable) on November 22, 2026.*


Start at the top row and work down, since each later flow reuses the pattern of the first.


### Set Up Each Shopify Airtable Workflow


Use "New Order" as the trigger and "Create Airtable Record" as the action, then map order number, total and email to fields. Test with one real order before mapping anything else.


Use "New Customer", then "Find Airtable Record" on the email field before "Create Airtable Record". Skipping the lookup is how duplicates get in.


When a product changes, "Updated Product" feeds "Update Airtable Record".


For stock going the other way, Airtable's "New or Updated Record" trigger can drive Shopify's "Adjust Inventory Level". That matters because the[Activepieces Airtable piece](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/airtable) lists only two triggers, "New Record" and "New or Updated Record", so nearly all Airtable-to-Shopify work runs through those two.


Trigger on "New Paid Order", add a branch on the order total, and create the record only on the high-value path. A filtered Airtable view then becomes the queue.


### Steps the integrations don't list


6 triggers and 27 actions: that is what the[Activepieces Shopify piece](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/shopify) lists. Shopify can do far more than it can announce, so flows that start in Shopify are the constrained ones.


Airtable lists 2 triggers and 15 actions, so it's even thinner on the starting side. **Plan every flow around the trigger you need and check it exists before you build.**


Take refunds. None of the six Shopify triggers is a refund event.


Register a refund webhook in Shopify, point it at Activepieces's "Catch Webhook" trigger, and finish with "Update Airtable Record". If the destination step is also missing, "Send HTTP Request" calls the Airtable API directly.


A short trigger list only stays short if you wait for the vendor to lengthen it.


Activepieces has 750 integrations, a count taken from the` packages/pieces/community` directory of its MIT-licensed open source monorepo on GitHub rather than quoted as a marketing figure, and roughly 60% of them were contributed by the community rather than built in-house, so the community has contributed more integrations than the in-house team.


If a Shopify refund trigger is the integration you need, you can generate it with AI and add it privately to your own instance without waiting on a release.


See the chart that follows for this imbalance across both integrations.
